svg.aria-label: The aesthetic of gold: transformation, perception and spirit, looping back to practice
svg.title: The aesthetic of gold — transformation, perception, spirit
svg.desc: Three panels. 1 Transformation: gold goes from alloyed ore through fire, hammering and burnishing to luminous leaf, and the mind goes from hindered through practice to luminous, following AN 5.23. 2 Perception: a lamp in a dark ground strikes gold leaf; only an eye at the mirror angle sees the glow, so the surface changes as the viewer moves. 3 Spirit: five readings (luminosity, incorruptibility, refinement, placelessness, preciousness) each with a practice, and a shadow side answered by using gold sparingly. A loop returns from spirit to practice.
svg.text: What the metal undergoes → what the eye meets → what traditions read in it → what returns to practice
in the metal and in the mind
gold as an event, not an object
same words for refined gold and a freed
only as bright as the room it is in
shifts as eye, lamp and day move — Pentcheva
seems self-lit on dark — Procopius, Tanizaki
flat leaf cancels depth — the gold ground
gold ground, Pure Land: heaven as no-where
→ loosen the grip of measured space
offering and merit — sutras written in gold
gold taken as the sacred itself: idol, vanity
golden calf · Jerome · Bernard of Clairvaux
read, then practised: the painting becomes the trace of this refinement
Shinsei: cultivation runs inward first; the viewer's resonance is a consequence, not a goal
